chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Shu'ayb, from al-Harithi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who died and left a female slave, having manumitted one-third of her, and the executor married her before any part of the inheritance was divided: that she is appraised, and she and her husband are compensated from the remainder of her price after she is appraised; and whatever of manumission or slavery befalls the woman applies to her child.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a partially manumitted female slave whose executor marries her before the inheritance is divided?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural mechanics of manumission when an executor (*wasi*) marries a partially freed slave woman before the estate's final distribution. By appraising her value and compensating the estate for the remaining share, the ruling ensures that the legal transition of her status—whether to full freedom or continued servitude—is definitively established, thereby determining the *umm al-walad* status of any offspring she bears.
